metaDescription: Recovery Pilot, Expand, and Enterprise. Start with Supplier/AP or Reconciliation. Prove Verified Value. Then expand.
heroTitleLine1: Start where the value is clearest.
heroLead: Begin with one defined recovery scope. Expand as RADR proves the economics.
heroSupport: Choose Supplier / AP, Reconciliation, or both.

how.title: Price follows the operating surface.
how.lead: Not seats. Not tokens. Not per-Decision credits.

locations.title: Locations
locations.body: How much of the operation RADR covers.

scope.title: Operating scope
scope.body: The operational complexity RADR is responsible for understanding.

responsibility.title: Decision responsibility
responsibility.body: Whether RADR recommends, prepares, or governs.

pilot.title: Choose your first recovery scope.
pilot.lead: 14 days to find and action recoverable value. Open cases stay on RADR until resolved, verified, or closed.
pilot.body: Choose Supplier/AP, Reconciliation, or both. 2–3 locations. Evidence from the systems you already run.
points: Open cases until resolved, verified, or closed

core.name: Expand
core.line: Expand from recovery into recurring Decisions across the operation.
core.audience: Connect the operation. Make better Decisions. Verify what changed.

control.name: Enterprise
control.audience: Coordinate, approve and learn across the group.

enterprise.body: For larger groups we can scope SSO / SAML, custom RBAC, warehouse connections, custom APIs, security review, data policies, custom onboarding, dedicated support, SLA and multi-entity deployment.

packagesNote: Start, Expand, and Enterprise are scoped to your operation.

prove.label: Start
prove.title: Prove recoverable value.
prove.body: A Recovery Pilot on Supplier/AP and/or Reconciliation — measurable Verified outcomes.

deploy.label: Expand
deploy.title: Make RADR the Decision layer.
deploy.body: More locations, Decision classes, and connected evidence.

scale.label: Enterprise
scale.title: RADR at group scale.
scale.body: Policies, approvals, governance, and enterprise controls.

compare.title: What changes as RADR takes on more.

items.q: What if a supplier takes longer than 14 days?
items.a: RADR keeps the case open until it resolves or is closed.

items.q: Do we have to replace our accounting or procurement stack?
items.a: No. RADR is designed to work across the systems already in use.
Not unless explicitly permitted by policy. Material external actions can remain approval-gated.

items.q: How does RADR define Verified Value?
items.a: Only when downstream evidence supports the economic outcome — for example a credit applied and matched to the original invoice.
Pricing depends on locations, operating scope and the level of Decision responsibility RADR takes on.

items.q: Can we start with one recovery scope?
items.a: Yes. The Margin Recovery Pilot is the preferred starting point — often 2–3 locations on a defined financial problem.

items.q: Do we need all our systems connected first?
items.a: No. Start with invoices, contracts, and AP evidence where available. Expand as more systems come online.
Yes. Recovery is where RADR starts. The same Decision system can extend into broader operating Decisions.
Yes. Larger groups can scope advanced controls, security, custom integrations, SLA and multi-entity deployment under Enterprise.

readyLead: Tell us what you run, where margin disappears, and which systems hold the evidence. We will scope the right place to start.

progression.title: Start → Expand → Enterprise.
progression.lead: Pricing scales with the operating scope RADR takes on.
